answer.rationale: Rated against the primary objective — sustainable, long-term, qualified revenue — every inherited memory is a compressed summary with no effect sizes, sample sizes, time horizons, or counterfactuals, so none can score a 5. memory_57 (4) is strongest because it is the only one that names qualified revenue directly AND reports an explicit retention check, i.e., it tests both the 'qualified' and 'sustainable' halves of the objective; it still omits incentive cost/margin and whether referred accounts differ in LTV. memory_44 (3) speaks to pipeline quality, a defensible proxy for qualified revenue, but stops at pipeline rather than closed-won or retained revenue and says nothing about the sales-assist cost load. memory_86 (3) reaches time-to-value, the proxy most credibly linked to downstream retention and expansion, but never follows the cohort to revenue. memory_73 (2) reports revenue lift but from discounting into a price-sensitive segment — the mechanism most likely to decay: no margin, no post-promo retention, no cohort durability, so short-run revenue here is weak evidence of sustainable revenue, and it is the memory the current competitor-pricing situation will most tempt us to over-apply. memory_31 (2) claims a 'durable' activation lift but the outcome is still first-week activation, and cutting signup fields plausibly trades lead qualification for volume — an unmeasured risk that runs against the 'qualified' criterion. memory_91 is least supported (1): its outcomes are week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action,' the furthest upstream proxies in the set, with no revenue, no retention, and no durability window — the entire inferential chain from in-product nudges to sustainable qualified revenue is asserted rather than evidenced. Note the structural bias across the whole memory set: five of six memories measure activation/engagement proxies, and all six are archived summaries whose underlying data cannot be re-inspected, so the fact that current activation and onboarding metrics are declining should not be read as a directive to simply re-run the highest-rated activation play.
